analysis:
The only changed lines are in provider-swift/Tests/ClusterOnboardingChecks/OnboardingChecks.swift, head 1257-1262. They add test-only assertions for a new U.oneBuild(pinned:current:) helper in the cluster onboarding update flow. The helper requires both Macs to report the same new build before the pair re-plans after a coordinated update. I reviewed the supplied excerpts, base 1583-1780 and head 1-450. These contain no changed lines and no production code.

The test target is built with plain swiftc by run.sh. It uses scripted operations with no provider, no network and no model. It does not touch the coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), the attestation chain (TB-009), App Attest authorization (TB-011), the local hold socket (TB-012) or the prefix cache (T-041). No keys, tokens, prompts or credentials are handled. The tests include checks that transcripts contain no credential, host name, address or SSH text. Those checks tighten, not weaken, data-exposure expectations.

Caveat: the production implementation of oneBuild is not in the supplied units, so I could not check its logic. The tests assert that a mismatched or unanswered peer build means wait, and that an empty setup means no plan. That is consistent with fail-safe behavior, but the real function needs review in whichever source file implements ClusterOnboardingUpdate. The relevant risks are a plan or serve triggered on a mixed-build pair, and trust in a peer-reported build. No regression is evidenced in the supplied material.
